summary: The note presents case studies of small and medium enterprises that expanded internationally, from a Danish furniture designer to an Oregon craft beer collective. It shows that planning, local partnerships, technology, cultural adaptation, financing, learning from setbacks, and ongoing engagement drive successful global growth.
one_line: Case studies of SMEs across several countries show planning, partnerships, technology, cultural adaptation, and funding as keys to successful international expansion.
key_facts: Jensen & Marek, a boutique Danish furniture designer founded in 2017, found demand for its minimalist designs in Japan and Canada using customer data.
Rikke Jensen and Lukas Marek attended international expos and furniture fairs starting in early 2024, and had a clear expansion roadmap by September 2024.
Beaux Visage, a French organic skincare line founded by Marie-Claire Dubois in 2021, targeted South Korea and signed an exclusive agreement with a Seoul-based distributor by November 2023.
Beaux Visage started offering smaller product sizes because Korean consumers preferred trying samples before buying full-size products.
CodeBright, an Indian app startup founded in January 2023 by Aarav Patel and Priya Singh, used cloud computing for real-time collaboration with clients worldwide by mid-2024.

CodeBright built customized health and wellness apps for medium-sized health providers in Australia and the United Arab Emirates, complying with the Australian Privacy Principles and UAE Telecommunications Regulatory Authority standards.
Little Amigos, a Mexican toy brand established in 2022, worked with cultural experts and by end of 2024 was established in several European countries, launching eco-friendly toys in Germany.
InnovateAfrika, a Kenyan tech hub founded in 2023 by Kevin Mwangi and Nia Serengeti, used a crowdfunding campaign to open satellite offices in Estonia and Singapore.

La Dolce Vita, an Italian gelato company founded by Angelo Bianchi in 2022, struggled with preservation during transport to the Middle East, and by mid-2025 had developed new packaging and specialized logistics partners.
La Dolce Vita applied its preservation lessons to other tropical markets such as Southeast Asia.
CyberSecure, a Polish tech startup, expanded cybersecurity services to Japan and the Nordics by late 2024, using virtual cultural-sensitivity workshops and agile project management software.
CraftedBrews, a craft beer collective from Oregon, began exporting to Scandinavia in 2025 and used tasting events and limited-edition collaborations with local breweries in Denmark and Sweden.
